text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm seeing gradual memory growth on long streaming chats that include tool loops. Staging run with ~10 concurrent sessions drifts ~400MB over 30m, doesn't hit OOM but keeps climbing. Repro on master after last kernel-selection tweak.

aj: repro steps? which commit/build?

maria: master@a1b2c3f, runtime image rwd-inference:canary-2026-03-16. Repro script: long_streamer.py making alternating chat/tool calls (open/close tools). Attaching short log snippet: 

```
[2026-03-16T14:02:14Z] kv_cache: session=0x7f3a pages_retained=124 pages_pinned=84 bytes=860160
[2026-03-16T14:12:14Z] kv_cache: session=0x7f3a pages_retained=160 pages_pinned=120 bytes=1105920
[2026-03-16T14:32:14Z] kv_cache: session=0x7f3a pages_retained=220 pages_pinned=190 bytes=1515520
```

maria: The weird bit is pages_pinned keeps increasing even after sessions are idle.

infra-bot: :robot_face: deploy-hook: canary-2026-03-16 rolled to staging at 14:00 UTC

dena: Did we change warmup/pre-warm behavior recently? That could leave refs around if warmup path retains handles.

sam: I ran perf and a quick heapwalk. Hot spots point to kv_page_release being hit less frequently; warmup path does an early return on an allocation failure path that looks like it skips release. Extract from perf flame: 

```
kv_lookup -> kv_acquire -> kv_warmup_prefetch (hot) -> alloc_buffer -> early-return (errno EAGAIN)
// missing kv_page_release on that early-return path
```

aj: interesting. any minimal repro? can we flip off warmup?

maria: yes, toggling KV_WARMUP=false in runtime config keeps memory stable in the same 1h run. With warmup on it drifts.

alloc-trace-bot: alloc-trace: created trace traces/2102468100-warmup-repro.zip (33MB)

dena: sounds like a refcount leak in warmup prefetch. Could be related to the kernel selection change that added asynchronous prefetchs to improve cold latency. The async path may not fully clean up on EAGAIN.

sam: I grep'd the diff — PR #1349 added async prefetch and changed kv_page_acquire semantics. There's a <> path where `return nullptr` happened before drop_ref(page). I'll open a tiny PR to drop the ref.

aj: please also add an integration that runs the long_streamer harness for 2h in CI smoke (can run nightly) — we need to catch regressions early.

maria: I'm running a 2h staging run with the fix-from-sam applied locally; current graph shows flattened retention after ~20m. Will post graphs when done.

sam: PR up: #1354 — adds explicit release in async-warmup failure path and adds a unit test that simulates EAGAIN on prefetch. cc @dena @aj

dena: quick note — we should consider adding an alloc-trace assertion to detect >N pinned pages per session after a full close. That would have flagged this earlier.

aj: agree. add an alert + a nightly long-context job in observability. Also add a short explanation for SRE runbook.

maria: current numbers from the patched build (30m in): 

```
baseline: pages_retained=120 pages_pinned=80
patched: pages_retained=122 pages_pinned=81
no-warmup: pages_retained=118 pages_pinned=79
```

maria: looks acceptable. I'll keep the long run going. cc: @sam can you link the PR and changelog in this thread?

sam: linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1354 , changelog: Added fix for async warmup early-return refcount release.

aj: plan: merge PR after 24h staging run, flip canary in prod with 1hr watch, and roll out alert for pinned page regression. Owners: sam (fix), maria (long-run verification + graphs), dena (add alloc-trace assertion), aj (rollout + alert).

maria: thanks all — will drop final graphs and close the loop. :thumbsup:
